title: Sarah Shifted From Faith to Control
paragraphs: Sarah Shifted From Faith to Control
Sarah did not fall all at once.
She drifted.

Not into open rebellion.
Not into wild sin.
Into something quieter. More respectable. More dangerous.
Control.

At first, it looked wise. Responsible, even. She planned every step, guarded every outcome, and held every burden with white-knuckled hands. She still said the right things. Still looked faithful on the outside. But deep within, trust in God was slowly being replaced by trust in herself.
And that is where many souls break without realizing it.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Control can wear the costume of obedience while hiding the heart of unbelief.

Sarah once knew how to wait. She once knew how to pray. She once knew how to surrender what she could not carry. But pain changed her rhythm. Delays tested her. Silence unsettled her. So instead of resting in the will of God, she began managing what only God could govern.
Read that again.
She was no longer living from faith. She was surviving by control.
And maybe that is where you are too.

You still believe in God, but you no longer trust Him with timing.
You still quote Scripture, but anxiety is making your decisions.
You still call it wisdom, but underneath it is fear dressed in religious language.
That is not a small issue. That is a heart issue.
Because the deeper sin beneath control is this: refusing to let God be God.
Sarah’s hands stayed busy because her heart had stopped bowing.
And when faith dies in practice, control takes the throne.

Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this is the kind of battle many people miss because it does not look dark at first. It looks organized. Disciplined. Strong. Yet beneath it is the ancient lie from Eden—that life works better when we take over.
That lie never leads to peace.

It leads to exhaustion.
It leads to striving.
It leads to spiritual dryness.
It leads to carrying weights your soul was never designed to bear.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.
And the library keeps growing almost daily:
But the story does not end with Sarah trapped in herself.
This is where the Gospel enters.

Because the answer to control is not “try harder to relax.”
The answer is Jesus Christ.

Sarah’s problem was not merely stress. It was sin. She had placed herself where only God belongs. She had trusted her own grasp more than His grace. And every one of us has done the same in one form or another. Scripture says whatever is not from faith is sin, and sin always separates us from the life of God.
That is the breaking point.

Not that Sarah was overwhelmed.
That she had turned from surrender.
That she needed more than a better system.
She needed repentance.
So do we.

And this is the glory of the Gospel: Jesus did not come for people who had everything under control. He came for sinners. He came for the fearful, the striving, the self-reliant, the burdened. At the cross, Christ bore not only obvious sins, but also the hidden sins we baptize with softer names—pride, unbelief, self-rule, control.

He died.
He rose.
He reigns.
And now grace calls Sarah back—not to techniques, but to trust.

Not to performance, but to surrender.
Not to self-salvation, but to redemption through Christ alone.
This is the holy exchange: Sarah releases the illusion of control, and Jesus gives her what control never could—peace with God.
Real peace.
The kind that does not come from certainty about outcomes, but from confidence in the Savior.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You cannot hold tightly to control and fully rest in grace at the same time.
One of them has to die.

And if today the Holy Spirit is exposing the places where you have gripped your life harder than you have trusted your Lord, do not harden your heart. Repent. Bring the fear into the light. Bring the striving into the light. Bring the hidden unbelief into the light.

Jesus is not asking you to save yourself.
He is calling you to come undone before Him and be made new.
Follow the source for deeper truth. Read slowly. Pray honestly.
So here is the question:
Where has control replaced trust in your life?
Because faith begins where self-rule ends.
